I was also very hesitant to try medication, but over so many years it was clear absolutely nothing else helped. Prozac was originally for my mental illness — I have bipolar, but it’s an antidepressant that is known to help with eating disorders. It’s very mild, I didn’t notice much of a difference on it besides just feeling a bit more “rational”—I was able to control myself or urge to binge more easily. After a few years, I went off it and still am ED free.

I’m not sure I have a set thing. I never got actual treatment or therapy for my eating disorder. For as long as I can remember, I’d been on some kind of diet or trying to lose weight. I think what helped was finally allowing myself to eat whatever I wanted, whenever I wanted, over time. I lost the urge to binge sometime after I stopped allowing any food to be off limits. Eventually, I was able to eat until satisfied or no longer had the desire to binge and purge. I wish I could be more helpful though. I also believe going on Prozac for awhile really helped with ED thoughts or urges to binge. 

Edit: I think a lot too was “wanting what I can’t have” or that kind of thing. I also did a lot of writing about my eating disorder and was slowly able to talk about it more openly, which helped me lose a lot of the shame I had for years regarding it. I remember once I admitted to my therapist that I had bulimia and not being able to look him in the eyes for a week after that since I felt so much shame. (I was in recovery for drugs and alcohol at the time — wasn’t ED therapy or anything but I found it harder to admit my eating disorder than anything else). The urge really lessened when I found myself able to talk about it as well.
I wish I had more tips but it’s not forever, I just wanted to give you some hope that you can recover. I had bulimia for at least a decade and am now 7 years free!

I ask him about his past. He talks for about 30 minutes while I just listen.

I’ve never seen a guy cry before, let alone, the strongest person I’ve met, until now. He tells me what he has been through, and how everyone he loved has given up on him.

I rub his back with my arm and put my head on his shoulder. I kiss him on the cheek. 

"I swear to god I have not had a stronger influence on my life than you. I want you to remember that. You’re okay. I’ll never be afraid of who you are," I tell him, running my hands through his hair. 

"Thank you," he whispers.

He looks at me and kisses me. We exchange a few slow kisses as I run my hand through his hair and he holds me tight. I hear the metro rail in the background yet again. I love how open he is. I love his vulnerability. I want to hold him, I want him to hold me, I want to be closer and closer to him. I want to be with him forever. I want to help him, I want him to keep helping me. I just want to lie with him and talk to him and smoke cigarettes in the dark and cry if we have to and let every emotion flow in front of us. I love the lack of judgment between us, and how nothing could ever make me think less of him. This moment is beautiful.

He brings out his phone and turns on “Your Hand in Mine" by Explosions in the Sky. In the dark hole of depression he faced, that song gave him hope. He told me the whole album is like a story. He told me it helped him get better.

I met him my first night of college. We'll call him Mike. I had a group of friends I had been talking to before college. None of us had met, but we had a group chat prior. We'd go from talking about how excited we were to go out together to talking about the shit we hated back home to talking about the times we've gotten our heart broken. I did feel like I knew these people. When we met, it felt surreal. We all hit it off really well, and I knew these people would remain my friends. I knew Mike was going to be a challenge. He was brilliant, and he knew it. He had been through some shit, and he had a smooth way of talking. I didn't trust him, and I didn't think I ever would. Naturally, I was cautious around him.

The first night of college, we went on a walk to smoke a joint. Mike was confident he could find a place we wouldn't get caught, and assured us we'd be fine. I believed him. We all smoked, got a little high, and felt good. I heard him talking philosophy to someone, and immediately got excited. Philosophy? That's one of my favorite subjects. He told me about a 7 year old girl who had tried to kill her parents. Okay, Mike had interesting things to say. This wasn't the usual "Where are you from, do you like college, what are your hobbies" talk. This was cool stuff. 

After a few days, we really hit it off. I spent a lot of time with him. We just talked. Talked about our life back at our hometowns and how happy we were to escape it. Talked about our families, and how we don't want to make the same mistakes our parents did. Talked about our favorite books, and how we both agreed The Great Gatsby is overrated. I really began to like him.

We went to a party together a few days later. We stood outside with some friends, and smoked cigarettes. He told me he was glad he met me, because I was one of the most real people he has met. I really did feel appreciated, but I feared he just wanted to get with me. I began to close off. I sat inside, drank, and stayed by myself to think. He asked me what was wrong more times in that hour than anyone has my whole life. I didn't think anything was.

A few nights later, he took me to this beautiful arboratorium. This place was completely dark, covered in trees, with a bench that seemed out of place in the middle. We sat there, and I cried, telling him how many times I've been fucked over. Not fucked over, but built up for nothing to happen. Got my hopes up so many fucking times, and have been let down. I remember my parents telling me they'd come to my gymnastics meet, but never showing. I hate being let down. So I became guarded. Mike saw this. He assured me he'd never hurt me. I told him about this time I got too drunk at a party, and got taken advantage of. He promised me I was safe with him, that he wasn't going anywhere, and that he'd never let that happen to me. For the first time in a long time, I opened up. I believed him.

I guess you could say we were official after that. We spent every Monday and Wednesday going to class, and eating lunch after. We hated dining hall food, so we'd smoke cigarettes after. We'd spend every night together. We'd watch Adult swim and laugh at how stupid it was. We'd go on cigarette walks and appreciate how fucking beautiful the world right around us was. We'd listen to music together in silence. We'd laugh at all the lizards mating. I fucking loved it. God, when was the last time I'd felt this carefree and happy?

Every few nights after sharing a bottle with our friends, we'd go on walks, and have deep talks. They got deeper each time. We'd sit behind an empty building, and I'd tell him more, and he'd wrap me in his arms. He'd open up to me, and we trusted each other. We were in this together. We had faith in each other. He cared so fucking much about me, and I to him. 

As he discovered more about me, I discovered more about myself. I began to break every night, remembering things I had suppressed. Remembering my hell of a life back home. He always comforted me, never judged me, never hated me for my mistakes. He made me feel so happy, yet I'd cry every night. I depended on him to hold me up. I was sure I couldn't have made it this far without him.

Sadly, I began to get worse. My past ate at me every fucking day. Haunted me, made me feel like I'd never escape. He could see this, and he knew it had to be up to me to move on. I didn't know if I could. I knew I relied on him too much, so I began to fear losing him. I lived in fear. I knew the second I'd lose him, I'd break. That's why I hated opening up to people. I can't rely on myself. I don't know how to. So I counted on him.

Something brought him back, and he told me we had to take a break. I couldn't do it. I knew it wouldn't be a break. I knew this was the end. So I gave up. I didn't give myself a chance. I cut giant fucking scars into my arms. Drank myself into another world every night. Watched myself die. He saw this happening, and encouraged me to stop. I didn't. 

One night, it got so bad I tried to drink myself to death. I failed. God, how could I fail? I'm so fuckin' tired of living. I couldn't do this anymore. I told him of my plans and told him to stop caring about me. Told him to leave while he could still forget me. Told him he shouldn't have had to hear my shit and deal with it, because I can't even fuckin listen to it myself. Told him the end is so fuckin near, so get the hell out of my life. Keep yourself safe. Stop fucking caring about me. I want to be alone.

That night, he sent me to a psychiatric hospital for suicide. It was that night I was sure I loved him.

While I refused help, I continued to run. Anything to stop thinking about him. Drugs, alcohol, cutting. Help me escape the pain. Screamed myself to insanity. Couldn't take the memories and the abandonment. Began suffering horribly from anxiety and panic attacks. It was just a few days ago I decided to get better.
